messages:
jess.b: Quick note — copied the sample app into a small workshop and students hit RuntimeError: Event loop is closed after server reloads. Minimal repro attached.

jess.b: using Python 3.11, httpx 0.24.1, uvicorn 0.21.1. We create client at module import: `client = AsyncClient()` then use it in handlers.

noah.w: that pattern is fragile. AsyncClient binds to the loop it was created on; when uvicorn reloads or pytest spins new loops the underlying transports get closed.

sam.k: yeah, common footgun. Workarounds: create client inside the lifespan/startup handler or use `async with AsyncClient():` and store on app.state.

jess.b: can we make the SDK less copy-paste friendly for the wrong pattern? Suggestion: add a helper like `AsyncClient.for_lifespan()` which returns an async context manager and docs that show the lifespan pattern. Also typing: our wrapper's `__aenter__` is currently `-> Any` so pyright complains.

sam.k: good idea. For typing, implement `async def __aenter__(self) -> "AsyncClient":` and inherit `typing.AsyncContextManager["AsyncClient"]` in the wrapper so tools know the right type.

noah.w: also add a short note in sample-app README: "Don't create AsyncClient at import time — use lifespan" and a tiny code snippet. New users copy those examples verbatim.

jess.b: filed gist with repro and failing logs: https://gist.github.com/jess/repro-async-client-loop-err

devx-bot: Created issue RDW-901: "py-sdk: add AsyncClient.for_lifespan helper + fix async context manager typing" (assigned to sam.k). :robot_face:

sam.k: I'll pick this up. Plan: add `AsyncClient.for_lifespan()` that returns an AsyncContextManager, update wrapper typing, and update the sample-app examples + README. Also add a short section in "testing" about pytest-asyncio/anyio and avoiding import-level clients.

jess.b: thanks! that'll save a lot of confused beginners. :+1:

noah.w: optional: consider a lint rule/snippet in devex checklist to flag `AsyncClient()` at module scope. low priority but could prevent future copy-paste.

sam.k: noted. I'll add it to the issue as a follow-up.
